newsitem.title: EGYPT: Five dead in Egypt as police, militants clash.
newsitem.headline: Five dead in Egypt as police, militants clash.

text.p: Four suspected Moslem militants and one policeman were shot dead on Wednesday after a 400-strong police force clashed with the Islamist gunmen in southern Egypt, security sources said.
They said two policemen and a passer-by were injured in the gunbattle in the vast fields around Nazlet el-Badraman village more than 240 km (150 miles) south of Cairo.
The sources said Minya police had been tipped off that the militants were hiding in the fields.

They rushed to the area early on Wednesday with two armoured personnel carriers but the militants -- believed to be members of the Gama'a al-Islamiya fighting for the last four years to overthrow the government -- hid in the palm trees and were able to kill policeman Salamah Ghoneim and wound the other two.
The police then fired at the tree tops, sending the bodies of the militants, which included a former police officer and three other government employees, tumbling to the ground.
Security crackdowns have managed to limit the activities of the Gama'a to southern Egypt and especially in the area around Mallawi town which is about 260 km (160 miles) south of Cairo.
Almost 1,000 people have been killed and scores wounded in the Islamist-sparked political violence.
